hypothesis: A Wilson finite-field (211,6,1) difference family, with its seven base blocks independently translated and normalized into integer rows, contains a scope-111 (7,5)-DTS.
rationale: The target needs seven six-mark rows and 105 distinct positive differences. A (211,6,1) difference family has seven six-element blocks whose 210 directed differences cover every nonzero residue exactly once. Independent cyclic translations preserve this modular uniqueness; exhaustively testing all primitive-root construction choices and translations determines whether the family admits seven ordinary rows contained in an interval of length 111.
expected_information_gain: A dual-verifier-accepted scope-111 witness would be true-objective progress from a finite-field construction. If no witness exists, the exhaustive screen will close this specific Wilson difference-family-to-integer-DTS transfer and report its best exact scope without implying global DTS infeasibility.
method: Implement the exact Wilson 1972 construction used by Sage's df_q_6_1 for prime field F_211: enumerate primitive roots x, derive r=x^70 and xx=x^5, enumerate all c satisfying the five-coset condition, and form seven blocks {xx^i, xx^i r, xx^i r^2, xx^i c, xx^i c r, xx^i c r^2}. Deduplicate equivalent block families. For every block, enumerate all 211 cyclic translations, normalize each translated set to a sorted row beginning at zero, and exhaustively pack one row per block with disjoint ordinary difference sets. Validate every best and target packing with the repository integer verifier and the independent flat-counter verifier.
metric: primitive roots, valid Wilson parameters, unique families, translation-normalized row options, exact packings, best verified scope, target witnesses, and dual-verifier validity
metric_relation_to_true_objective: A complete seven-row assignment accepted by both independent verifiers with scope<=111 is exactly a true-objective witness. A best scope above 111 or a family closure is structural evidence only.
kill_condition: Stop at the first dual-verifier-accepted scope-111 witness or after exhausting all primitive-root/c choices, deduplicated Wilson families, translations, and exact row packings. Do not infer global DTS infeasibility from this finite construction family.

baseline_comparison.expected_relation: strict improvement only if complete and dual-verifier-valid

previous_best_comparison.expected_relation: new Wilson finite-field difference-family transfer, not a solver or local-repair repeat

interpretation: The exhaustive Wilson finite-field screen found no target witness. Its best complete ordinary DTS has scope 153 and is accepted by both independent verifiers, so this family is structurally valid but far from the frozen scope-111 target.
what_was_learned: All 48 primitive roots and 576 valid Wilson parameters collapsed to 24 block families; all seven blocks in each family had their complete translation-normalized option sets screened by exact disjoint-difference packing. No scope-111 packing exists in the tested family orbit, while the best valid scope is 153. This closes the tested Wilson transfer without implying DTS infeasibility.
recommended_next_action: Close this Wilson difference-family transfer. Do not spend more compute on its cyclic translations or equivalent primitive-root orbit; resume only with a materially different structural construction or stronger capability.
repetition_justification: This is a new finite-field difference-family construction and transfer mechanism. It is distinct from the previously tested Ruzsa modular ruler split, polynomial gap families, random catalogues, SAT encodings, and repair searches.
